questions.question: The Supreme Court has special advisory jurisdiction in matters which may specifically be referred to it by the President of India under Article ____ of the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 143**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article **143** of the **Indian Constitution** grants the **Supreme Court of India** special advisory jurisdiction in matters specifically referred to it by the **President of India**. 
 
• The President can seek the Supreme Court's opinion on questions of law or fact that arise out of public importance, 
 
 
• and the Court may offer its advisory opinion in such cases.
 
 
 
• This power allows the President to consult the highest judicial authority for guidance on constitutional matters and other significant legal issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 141**:

 
 
• **States that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.**
 
• It **Promotes consistency in the application of laws and ensures the supremacy of the Supreme Court as the interpreter of the Constitution.**
 
• This ensures uniformity in the interpretation of laws across the country.
 
• The judgments of the Supreme Court set precedents that lower courts must follow (Doctrine of Precedent).
 
 
 
• **Article 142**:
 
 
• Grants the Supreme Court the power to pass any order or decree for doing complete justice in any case.
 
• **This article gives the Court extraordinary powers to ensure justice prevails, even in cases where existing laws or technicalities may fall short.**
 
• The Supreme Court has used this article in landmark cases such as:
 
• **Union Carbide Corporation v. Union of India (Bhopal Gas Tragedy case)** to ensure fair compensation.
 
• **Babri Masjid case** for the amicable resolution of disputes.
 
 
 
• **Article 144**:
 
 
• Directs all authorities, civil and judicial, in India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.
 
• **This article ensures the enforceability of the Supreme Court’s decisions and directives**.
 
• It mandates that courts and other institutions cooperate with the Supreme Court in administering justice.

questions.question: This festival belongs to Sambalpur (Western Odisha), the new harvest crops are worshipped and people celebrate it by eating the first rice of the harvest together with their family:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nuakhai**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nuakhai is an agricultural festival celebrated by the people of Odisha.

 
 
• It is the greatest harvesting festival of Odisha.
 
• It is observed to welcome the new rice of the season.
 
• Nua means new and Khai means food i.e. Nuakhai's Hindi meaning is 'new food'.
 
• ‘Nuakhai’ festival is celebrated one day after the Ganesh Chaturthi festival.__
 
• The festival has a big significance for farmers and the agricultural community.
 
• The festival is observed on Panchami tithi (the fifth day) of the lunar fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada (August–September) as per the Hindu calendar
 
• ‘Nuakhai' is the most important social festival of Western Odisha.
 
• It is also celebrated in Southern Chhattisgarh.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84d9e48be03a0e5790e1bc4672e3f928c3e9b3c5716792f17f381aeeb1670453.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Baisakhi**:

 
 
• It is **Celebrated primarily in Punjab**, this festival marks the beginning of the harvest season and also commemorates the formation of the Khalsa in 1699.
 
• Traditionally, Baisakhi marks the end of the harvest season and is a time of great joy and festivity for farmers.
 
• Punjab and Haryana are the states where the celebrations are concentrated.
 
• There are many names for this festival, including Pohela Baishakhi in West Bengal, Bohag Bihu in Assam, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, Phool Dei in Uttarakhand, Ugadi in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, Pooram Vishu in Kerala and Mahavishuva Sankranti in Odisha
 
 
 
• **Vishu**:
 
 
• Vishu, a Hindu festival, is celebrated in Kerala as the harvest festival and the astrological New Year of the Malayalis.
 
• Vishu indicates the movement of the sun to Aries or the Mesha Rashi and marks the day from which the farmers begin the plowing of land and other agricultural activities.
 
• In Sanskrit, Vishu means equal, which implies the day with an equal number of hours of day and night or the equinox.
 
• The day of Mesha Sankranti or Mesha Sankramam, Vishu is a family festival.
 
 
 
• **Bohag Bihu**:
 
 
• It is **Celebrated in Assam**,
 
• It **marks the Assamese New Year **
 
• **It **is **also a harvest festival.**

questions.question: ____ are organized institutions that accept deposits from depositors and advance loans to borrower.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banks**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banks** are financial institutions that accept deposits from customers (depositors) and provide loans to individuals, businesses, or other entities (borrowers).
 
• Banks **play a crucial role in the economy by facilitating the flow of money and credit,**
 
• It helps ** with savings, investments, and facilitating economic growth through lending.**
 
• They offer a range of services, including savings accounts, current accounts, fixed deposits, and loans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 
 
 

 Types of Banks
 Meaning
 
 

 **Scheduled Banks**
 
 
 
• They are described in the Reserve Bank of India Act as banks that are listed in the 2nd schedule of the RBI Act of 1934.
 
• All the RRBs, Indian and foreign commercial banks, and cooperative banks are considered scheduled banks.
 
• Scheduled banks must have a minimum paid-up capital and reserves of up to INR 25 lakh.
 
 
 
 

 **Non-Scheduled Banks**
 
 
 
• These banks do not follow the 2nd schedule of the RBI Act of 1934, and hence they are not bound to the RBI guidelines.
 
• They are required to maintain a Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), not with the RBI but by themselves.
 
• Non-scheduled banks have a paid-up capital of less than INR 5 lakhs.
 
 
 
 

 **Commercial Banks**
 
 
 
• A commercial bank is one that primarily deals with accepting deposits and lending loans to their customers.
 
• They are financial entities providing facilities to individuals, businesses, and organizations in the form of current, deposit, and savings accounts. They also provide loans to businesses.
 
• They can be either scheduled or non-scheduled.
 
 
 
 

 **Public Sector Banks**
 
 
 
• The government owns the majority of the shares of such banks. The ownership of the government is generally more than 50%. For instance, the government share of the State Bank of India (SBI) is 58.60%, while that of the Punjab National Bank (PNB) is 58.87%.
 
• These banks are further classified into Nationalized Banks and State Bank and its Associates.
 
 
 
 

 **Private Sector Banks**
 
 
 
• The majority of the equity is held by private entities, corporations, institutions, or individuals along with the government.
 
• Banking in India has been dominated by public sector banks since 1969 when all the major banks were nationalized by the Indian government.
 
• After liberalization in the 1990s, banks like ICICI, HDFC, etc. became the new age private sector banks.
 
• Currently, there are 22 private-sector banks operational in the country.
 
 
 
 

 **Foreign Banks**
 
 
 
• These banks are compelled to follow the guidelines of both the home as well as the host countries.
 
• Such banks tend to be more effective in countries with high taxes and nations where it is easy for international firms to enter the market.
 
• Currently, there are a total of 46 foreign banks operational in India.
 
 
 
 

 **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**
 
 
 
• These banks were established in 1975 following the recommendations of “The Narasimham Committee” under the RRB Act 1976.
 
• These banks are regulated and supervised by the NABARDs (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)
 
• RRBs are owned by 3 entities Central Government (50%), State Government (15%), and Sponsor Banks (35%)
 
• There are a total of 56 RRBs currently operational in the country.
 
 
 
 

 **Cooperative Banks**
 
 
 
• These are important forms of carrying out business through mutual understanding.
 
• Cooperative banks play a very important role in the rural economy development of the country.
 
• The rural cooperative credit sector which accounted for over 50% of the credit disbursed a few years back, now has less than 20% shares.

questions.question: The system of the mahalwari settlement was devised by ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holt Mackenzie**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Mahalwari Settlement was devised by Holt Mackenzie and Robert Merttins Bird in 1822.**
 
• The **Mahalwari Settlement was a combination of the Permanent Settlement and the Ryotwari System. **
 
• **Mahalwari Settlement**:
 
 
• The **land was divided into Mahals**, with each Mahal consisting of one or more villages. 
 
• The **peasants owned the land. **
 
• The village committee was responsible for collecting taxes. 
 
• The Lambardar, a head of the village, collected revenue. 
 
• The **Mahalwari Settlement was created to protect the rights of peasant proprietors and maximize revenue. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Thomas Munro:**

 
 
• He is **known for introducing the Ryotwari System o**f land revenue in Madras Presidency (modern Tamil Nadu).
 
• This s**ystem directly taxed the cultivators (ryots) instead of intermediaries.**
 
• He played a key role in administrative reforms and promoting education during his tenure as Governor of Madras (1820–1827).
 
 
 
• A**lexander Read:**
 
 
• He is **Credited with laying the groundwork for the Ryotwari System in small parts of Baramaha**l (modern Tamil Nadu) before Thomas Munro expanded it.
 
• He **introduced measures to simplify land revenue collection and provide relief to farmers in areas affected by famine.**
 
 
 
• **Richard Wellesle**y:
 
 
• He was **Governor-General of India (1798–1805).**
 
• He is Associated with the **expansion of British territories in India through the Subsidiary Alliance policy.**
 
• He played a crucial role in defeating Tipu Sultan in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).
 
• He **established the Fort William College in Calcutta for training civil servants.**
 
• He Often referred to as the “Architect of British Empire in India.”

questions.question: The literacy rate is defined by the percentage of the population of a given age group that can ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Read and Write**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **literacy rate** is a measure of the percentage of people in a specific age group who can **read and write** with understanding, in any language. 
 
• It reflects the basic educational level of a population, indicating their ability to engage with written content effectively.
 
• These are fundamental skills for communication, education, and participation in society. It is not limited to reading or writing alone.
 
• Most countries and international organizations, including the UNESCO, define literacy as the ability to read and write simple statements or text in any language, even if the person is not fully fluent in that language.
 
• The literacy rate is typically calculated for individuals above a certain age, usually 15 years and older, to assess the educational attainment of a country or region.
 
• The standard definition of literacy may vary slightly depending on local contexts and educational systems, but the core concept remains the ability to **read and write**.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

A) Calcium is present in S-block of the periodic table.

B) Metals comprise more than 78% of all known elements and appear on the left side of the Periodic Table.

C) d- Block elements are also known as inner-transition electrons.

options.text: Both A and B is true
Only B and C is true
Both A and C is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B is true**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A) Calcium is present in S-block of the periodic table**.

 
 
• **This statement is True**.
 
• **Calcium (Ca) is an alkaline earth metal w**ith the atomic number 20.
 
• It is **located in Group 2 of the periodic table**, which is part of the S-block.
 
• The S-block consists of Groups 1 and 2 (alkali and alkaline earth metals).
 
 
 
• **B) Metals comprise more than 78% of all known elements and appear on the left side of the Periodic Table.**
 
 
• **This statement is True.**
 
• **Metals make up about 80% of the known elements in the periodic table.**
 
• They are primarily found on the left and centre of the periodic table, including the S-block, D-block, and part of the P-block.
 
 
 
• **C) d- Block elements are also known as inner-transition electrons.**
 
 
• **This statement is False.**
 
• **d-block elements are commonly known as transition metals, not inner-transition metals.**
 
• The inner-transition elements refer to the f-block elements, which include the lanthanides and actinides.
 
 
 
• Hence Both A and B are true

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Of the known elements in the periodic table, only 11 are gases under normal atmospheric conditions__.

 
 
• These gases are hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, chlorine, helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.
 
• The periodic table is managed by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, or IUPAC.
 
• The modern periodic table sorts the elements according to increasing atomic number instead of increasing atomic mass.
 
• There are 118 elements in a periodic table.
 
• There are seven periods and eighteen groups in the modern periodic table.

questions.question: National defence, roads, government administration are examples of which types of goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public goods**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Public goods** are those that are non-excludable and non-rivalrous. 

 
 
• This means that:

 
 
• **Non-excludable**: Once provided, no one can be excluded from using them.
 
• **Non-rivalrous**: One person’s use of the good does not reduce its availability for others.
 
 
 
 
 
• Public goods like **national defence**, **roads**, and **government administration** are essential services that benefit the entire population

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complementary Goods**:

 
 
• These are **goods that are used together, where the use of one increases the demand for the other (e.g., cars and petrol).**
 
• **Example**: Cars and petrol, printers and ink cartridges, or smartphones and apps.
 
• A rise in the price of one complementary good (e.g., petrol) may decrease the demand for the other (e.g., cars).
 
 
 
• **Private Goods**:
 
 
• Private goods are goods that are both **excludable** (producers can prevent people who do not pay for them from using them) and **rivalrous** (one person’s use of the good reduces its availability to others).
 
• **Example**: Food, clothing, and personal gadgets.
 
• **Excludability**: Producers can prevent non-payers from accessing the goods.
 
• **Rivalry**: Consumption by one individual reduces the availability for others
 
 
 
• ​** Supplementary Goods**:
 
 
• These are goods that can be used as alternatives to other goods, meaning their consumption is related to or in place of another (e.g., tea and coffee as substitutes).
 
• **Alternatives**: Consumers may choose one good over the other based on price or preference.
 
• **Impact on Demand**: A price increase in one will generally increase demand for its substitute.
 
• **Example**: Tea and coffee, butter and margarine.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saina Nehwal**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saina Nehwal** is one of India's most prominent **badminton players** and has achieved significant success in the sport, including:

 
 
• **Olympic Bronze Medalist** (2012 London Olympics).
 
• Multiple **Commonwealth Games Gold Medals**.
 
• Former **World No. 1** in women's singles badminton.
 
• She has won over **24 international titles**, including **10 Superseries titles**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Mary Kom**:

 
 
• Mary Kom, **also known as "Magnificent Mary**," is one of India’s most celebrated athletes and a trailblazer in women’s boxing.
 
• **Six-time world champion,** winning gold at the **AIBA World Boxing Championships across different weight categories.**
 
• Bronze medalist at the 2012 London Olympics, making her the first Indian woman boxer to achieve this feat.
 
• **Gold medalist at the 2014 Asian Games and the 2018 Commonwealth Games.**
 
• Only **woman boxer to win a medal in each of the first seven World Championships.**
 
• **Awarded the Padma Bhushan (2013), Padma Shri (2006), and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2009)**.
 
• She is also a Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and actively supports initiatives promoting sports in India.
 
 
 
• **Mithali Raj**:
 
 
• **Mithali Raj is an icon in Indian cricket and a pioneer in women's sports globally.**
 
• Highest run-scorer in women’s ODIs, with over 7,800 runs in her illustrious career.
 
• **First woman to score seven consecutive 50s in ODIs.**
 
• Captained India to two ICC Women’s World Cup finals (2005 and 2017).
 
• **The first Indian cricketer (male or female) to complete 20 years in international cricket.**
 
• Recipient of the Arjuna Award (2003), Padma Shri (2015), and the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2021).
 
 
 
• ** Sakshi Malik**:
 
 
• **Bronze medalist in the 58 kg freestyle wrestling category at the 2016 Rio Olympic**s, making her the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal.
 
• **Gold medalist at the 2017 Commonwealth Wrestling Championships.**
 
• Multiple-time medalist at Asian Wrestling Championships.
 
• **Awarded the Padma Shri (2017) and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2016)**

questions.question: In which sport would you perform a "smash" shot?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Badminton**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A "smash" shot is performed in badminton:** 
 
• A **smash is an offensive shot in badminton** where the player hits the shuttlecock with power and speed downward into the opponent's court.
 
• The **smash is typically executed from the rear court and can be played on either the forehand or backhand side.**
 
• The steep trajectory of the shuttlecock makes it difficult for the opponent to return.
